findings.reason: as written the node reports a causal story from substituted inputs as if it reproduced the record, which is exactly the defect this section exists to stop repeating; the method needs to mark each reconstructed input in the log and state that a reproduction resting on one is conditional, or the report's named cause cannot be trusted by the section that fixes it.
findings.text: s23's method loads, for each runtime input the picker reads (lane document, budget verdict, each serving probe), "the value recorded or nearest in time", and the done-where requires that the script "reproduces the recorded outcome of both attempts" and that the report "name, for each attempt, which inputs decided the refusal". A nearest-in-time lane document or serving probe is a value that may never have been in force at 02:29:07Z, so where a substituted input is the one that decides, the reproduction attributes the original refusal to a state the picker never read — the same failure that refuted the three earlier mechanisms this section records, and the section would carry it straight into the fix section it promises. The missing distinction is between a value that was recorded and one that was reconstructed.

findings.reason: naming the existing helper changes what the node writes and what its negative control must exercise; without it the accepted path and every dispatch path can disagree about whether a parked request binds.
findings.text: s24 asks the accept-path check to treat a claim held by a request in `queued`, `awaiting-upstream`, `blocked-upstream` or `held` as a stopped peer's. That rule already exists: `WAITING_REQUEST_PHASES` and `claim_disposition` at `reckon/crew/node.py:1529-1576` return `binding=False` for exactly those four phases with the reason "is {phase} and holds no worker or worktree, so its claim is disregarded", and `queue_admission.py:905`, `dispatch_claims.py:506`, `queue_edit.py:240` and `runs.py:1232` all reuse it. `promotion_scope.py` is the one claim walk that does not: it re-derives the decision from `stopped_with_terminal_manifest` and `_path_change_reaches_integration_head` (lines 603-665). Implementing s24 as another phase test in that function makes a fifth copy of one rule, and the three cases it proposes would pass against a rule that could later drift from the accepted one.
